name: Skeena26
approach: South Face is another wall within the same Squire Creek Walls complex as Waterfall Basin, reached via the same Darrington-area approach: I-5 to the Arlington exit, SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington, then Squire Creek Road to the washout-blocked parking area. From there, follow the same rough, unmaintained approach — the old roadbed past a landslide crossing, a faint trail through streambed and alder brush, a ford of Squire Creek, and obscure forest track — before breaking into the open basin roughly 2 hours from the car; South Face is one of the walls encountered within that same basin complex, with route-finding (flagging, cairns) required in several spots.

waypoints.name: Squire Creek Road washout parking (FS Rd 2040)
waypoints.directions: Take I-5 to the Arlington exit, then SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. From town, follow Squire Creek Road until it is blocked by the washout and park at the gated area there, around 1,200 feet. You cannot drive past that point; the climbers' path toward the Squire Creek Walls starts from the parking area, beginning on the old roadbed beyond the gate.

waypoints.name: Grassy saddle (South Face routes)
waypoints.note: Brilliant white slab starting near the saddle, mostly 5.4-5.6 with a 5.9 opening pitch.
waypoints.directions: Follow the old roadbed beyond the gate past the landslide crossing to two cut logs on either side of the road with old logging cable showing, where a boot track drops right toward the creek. Ford Squire Creek at its shallowest point, follow the climbers' track upstream across a tributary, then climb two steep, muddy gullies to the open grassy saddle below the wall.
